history.title: setup / foundation
history.account: The Raincut cooperative fitted out the store cavern because the group had no dependable place for material needed between supply journeys. The aim was to keep a shared reserve available through interruptions. The site was chosen because the enclosing rock protected stored goods from ordinary weather.

history.title: e1 / flood
history.account: Debris blocked a lower outlet; water from the runoff channel collected in a retained cavity below the dry surroundings.

history.title: e2 / block
history.account: The Raincut cooperative blocked a secondary connection to keep travelers off the unsafe approach, channeling visitors toward supervised access.

history.title: e3 / withdraw
history.account: The Raincut cooperative left because the unrepaired flood made continued occupation costly. The place was left vacant.

history.title: e4 / dispute
history.account: The Old Hearth claimants sought control of the protected storage space. They produced an older boundary agreement and claimed rights to the place; the claim remained unresolved.

history.title: e5 / collapse
history.account: A weather-exposed support failed under load and broke a service crossing.
